- 100% ownership of all subsidiaries ensures complete strategic alignment, governance control, and retention of entire embedded value/profitability within the Group across cycles.
- Diversified four-engine conglomerate model (Banking, Capital Markets, Asset Management, Protection) provides inherent counter-cyclical resilience and earnings stability.
- Strong capital position with standalone CET-1 ratio of 21.34% and consolidated CAR of 22.97%, providing strategic flexibility.
- Established brand and robust governance/risk management framework built over four decades, evidenced by 5-year BVPS CAGR of 16%.
- Integrated distribution combining physical branches evolving into 'One Kotak' destinations with digital and voice-assisted channels, enabling cross-selling and advisory-led engagement.
- Deep domain expertise in niche lending segments: ranked #2 in Tractor Finance and among top five in Commercial Vehicles and Construction Equipment finance.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Credit Risk â Asset Quality Deterioration — Credit risk is the most significant risk for the Group, arising from potential failure of borrowers or counterparties to meet obligations. Deterioration in repayment capacity, sector stress, or macroeconomic shocks could impair asset quality and profitability.
- Net Interest Margin (NIM) Compression — RBI reduced the policy repo rate by 100 basis points during the year, leading to NIM compression across the banking sector. Sustained low-rate environment or competitive pricing pressure could further compress margins.
- Regulatory and Compliance Risk — Regulatory constraints that had restricted certain digital onboarding and credit card business activities were lifted only in February 2025. Future regulatory actions or non-compliance could again restrict business capacity or impose penalties.
- Data Security and Privacy / Cyber Risk — Increasing reliance on digital channels and data-driven operations heightens exposure to cyber threats, data breaches, and service disruptions, which can lead to regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and loss of customer trust.
- Climate and ESG Integration Risk — Inadequate integration of climate and ESG risks in lending and investment decisions may affect credit quality and portfolio resilience. The Bank strengthened its Environmental and Social risk framework during the year, embedding it into credit decisions.
- Concentration Risk — Credit risk concentration is actively managed to prevent excessive exposure to individual borrowers, groups, sectors, or geographies. Breach of concentration limits could amplify losses in a downturn.
- Capital Adequacy and Stress Resilience — The Group maintains prudent buffers above regulatory minima, but adverse macroeconomic scenarios or unexpected losses could strain capital adequacy, requiring capital conservation or constraining growth.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Kotak Mahindra Bank provides a comprehensive suite of financial solutions across customer segments and geographies in India, anchored by four interconnected engines: Banking & Lending, Capital Markets, Asset Management, and Protection. The Group serves over 5.2 crore customers through a physical network of 5,581 locations and digital platforms, targeting HNIs, SMEs, Core India retail, and institutional clients. All subsidiaries are 100% beneficially owned by the Bank, enabling integrated product manufacturing and distribution while retaining full profitability within the Group.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Banking & Lending:** Kotak811 (digital banking), Solitaire (HNI proposition), Private Bank, SME Banking, Corporate Bank, Tractor Finance, Commercial Vehicles Finance, Construction Equipment Finance, Mortgage Loans
- **Capital Markets:** Investment Banking (KMCC), Institutional Equities, Broking (Kotak Securities), Kotak Neo (trading app)
- **Asset Management:** Domestic Mutual Funds (Debt & Equity), Offshore Funds, Alternate Assets, PMS, NPS
- **Protection:** Life Insurance (Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Limited (KMCC) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank; divested 30.99% of its stake in associate Infina Finance Private Limited on 24th March, 2026.
- Infina Finance Private Limited (Infina) — associate: Former associate of the Bank via KMCC; ceased to be an associate on 24th March, 2026 following KMCC's partial stake sale.
- Kotak Mahindra General Insurance Company Limited (KGI) / Zurich Kotak General Insurance Company India Limited (ZKGI) — associate: Former subsidiary; Bank divested 70% stake to Zurich Insurance Company Limited on 18th June, 2024, retaining 30% share capital. Entity renamed Zurich Kotak General Insurance Company India Limited.
- Kotak Mahindra Investments Limited (KMIL) — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; business activities to be conducted departmentally within the Bank from 1st April, 2026. KMIL will cease sanctioning new loans from that date while continuing to service existing facilities.
- Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance Company Limited — related party: Unlisted entity where Mr. C S Rajan serves as Independent Director and holds committee chairmanships/memberships.
- Vidya Bhawan Society — related party: CSR implementing partner for infrastructure development of Vidya Bhawan schools (project completed in FY 2025-26).
- Manav Sadhan Vikas Sanstha — related party: CSR implementing partner for construction and setting up of hostel facility (project completed in FY 2025-26).
- Mahindra United World College of India — related party: CSR implementing partner for construction and refurbishment of multiple facilities in educational institutions (project completed in FY 2025-26).
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- 100% ownership of all subsidiaries ensures complete strategic alignment, governance control, and retention of entire embedded value/profitability within the Group across cycles.
- Diversified four-engine conglomerate model (Banking, Capital Markets, Asset Management, Protection) provides inherent counter-cyclical resilience and earnings stability.
- Strong capital position with standalone CET-1 ratio of 21.34% and consolidated CAR of 22.97%, providing strategic flexibility.
- Established brand and robust governance/risk management framework built over four decades, evidenced by 5-year BVPS CAGR of 16%.
- Integrated distribution combining physical branches evolving into 'One Kotak' destinations with digital and voice-assisted channels, enabling cross-selling and advisory-led engagement.
- Deep domain expertise in niche lending segments: ranked #2 in Tractor Finance and among top five in Commercial Vehicles and Construction Equipment finance.
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Build a unified digital SME platform spanning sourcing, underwriting, credit and operations to improve turnaround time, operational efficiency and customer experience.
- Shift Corporate Banking toward a diversified, capital-efficient model by reducing reliance on spread-based income and scaling fee-based, transaction and flow-driven revenues.
- Prioritise granular, diversified growth in the Mid-Market segment, significantly faster than other segments, driven by new-to-bank customer additions and referral-led sourcing.
- Leverage Centres of Excellence for large corporates (Infrastructure Financing, Real Estate Financing, Financial Institutions, Financial Sponsors, Multi-National Companies, New-age Companies Banking) to deliver expertise and healthy profitability.
- Scale fee-led, capital-efficient niche businesses (Syndication & Debt Capital Markets, Custody Services, Asset Reconstruction) to enhance earnings quality and diversification beyond lending.
- Strengthen transaction banking franchise by deepening participation in customer flows through trade finance, supply chain solutions and cash management services.
- Execute a geography-led expansion strategy in Tractor and Farm Equipment, combining consolidation in mature markets with selective growth in underpenetrated regions.
- Deepen engagement with the venture capital ecosystem for early access to funded startups and maintain a fast-tracked credit framework for portfolio companies of leading VC firms.
- The Board proposed a dividend for the year ended 31st March, 2026, payable after shareholder approval at the Annual General Meeting. The Bank also executed a sub-division (split) of equity shares from face value of ₹5 to ₹1 effective 14th January, 2026, reflecting a shareholder-friendly capital management approach.
- Strengthened Environmental and Social (E&S) risk framework during the year, aligning with global standards and embedding it into credit decisions through policy enhancements and training.
- Embed ESG and climate risk assessment in credit processes, scenario analysis, and portfolio monitoring to enhance portfolio resilience.
- Reasonable Assurance obtained on BRSR Core as per SEBI guidelines; Limited assurance on additional select indicators.
- CSR applicable under Section 135 of Companies Act, 2013; community grievances received through NGO partners with no grievances reported in the period.
- Women representation on Board of Directors at 16.7% and in Key Management Personnel at 16.7%; permanent employee female representation at 32.2%.
- Differently abled permanent employees represent 85.3% male and 14.7% female of the differently abled employee base.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report does not describe specific new capacity, plant, or infrastructure expansion projects with commissioning timelines. The narrative focuses on scaling the franchise through organic growth in advances and deposits, supported by technology enhancements and the lifting of regulatory constraints on digital onboarding and credit card activities. The three strategic pillars—Focus Customer Segment Propositions, Independent Product Businesses within the Bank, and Technology, Digital & AI—are now fully aligned to enable seamless execution. Growth is led by SME, Mortgage, and Corporate Banking segments, with ongoing investments in technology and digital capabilities to support scalability.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and volatile business sentiment resulted in muted corporate credit demand in H1 FY26; activity improved in H2, particularly across wholesale trade, commercial real estate and lending to NBFCs.
- In an environment where the benchmark repo rate fell sharply, profitability was supported by pricing discipline and deeper participation in non-credit businesses.
- Sustained momentum in new business origination while maintaining stable spreads drove Corporate SME growth of 16.67% YoY.
- Healthy working capital demand across sectors supported Business Banking growth of 23.98% YoY.
- Deeper customer engagement, cross-sell, higher fee income and continued New-to-Bank acquisitions drove Agri SME growth of 15.43% YoY.
- Tractor industry grew 23.47% supported by favourable policy measures, subsidy support and positive monsoon conditions; the Bank pursued calibrated growth relative to industry momentum.
- Commercial Vehicles industry grew approximately 13% in unit terms, supported by GST-related pricing benefits and pre-buying ahead of anticipated OEM price revisions.
- Subdued offshore flows amid volatility were partly offset by strong domestic participation in the custody business.
- Credit substitute portfolio moderated in favour of the advances book reflecting interest rate movements in the market.
- Japan and Taiwan desks continued to build a strong pipeline for multinational companies.
- Real Estate Financing sustained momentum in new originations, supported by deep relationships with established developers and a diversified exposure profile, adding new-to-bank clients to strengthen the future pipeline.
- Syndication and Debt Capital Markets delivered healthy growth in debt placements and recorded fee income at an all-time high for the second consecutive year, with regulatory permission for acquisition financing expanding addressable opportunity meaningfully.
- Asset Reconstruction Division actively tracking opportunities across corporate and retail segments.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

open.item: Board recommended a dividend of ₹0.65 per equity share (face value ₹1) for FY 2025-26.
The Board recommended a dividend of H0.65 per equity share (Face Value of H1/-) for FY 2025-26.

Business activities of wholly-owned subsidiary Kotak Mahindra Investments Limited (KMIL) will be conducted departmentally within the Bank from 1st April, 2026; KMIL shall not sanction any new loans from that date while continuing to service existing facilities.

Execute strategy anchored on three pillars: Focus Customer Segment Propositions (HNI, Core India/Kotak811, SME, Institutional), Independent Product Businesses within the Bank (Tractor Finance, CV/CE), and Technology, Digital & AI.
Grow disproportionately and gain market share over time in four focus customer segments: HNI, Core India (Kotak811), SME, and Institutional.
The Bank's three strategic pillars—Focus Customer Segment Propositions, Independent Product Businesses within the Bank, and Technology, Digital & AI—are fully aligned, enabling seamless execution.
Growth in the credit substitute book is largely dependent on the movement of interest rates and pricing vis-à-vis loans.
The Corporate Bank expects the Financial Sponsors segment to be a significant lever in growth going forward.

New-Age Companies Banking is deepening engagement with the venture capital ecosystem for early access to funded startups and maintaining a fast-tracked credit framework for portfolio companies of leading VC firms.
Tractor and Farm Equipment business is executing a geography-led expansion strategy, combining consolidation in mature markets with selective growth in underpenetrated regions.
The Bank is strengthening its transaction banking franchise by increasing participation in customer flows through trade finance, supply chain solutions and cash management services.
The Mid-Market segment is being grown significantly faster than other segments, prioritising granular, diversified growth.
Corporate Banking is shifting toward a diversified and capital-efficient model, reducing reliance on spread-based income while scaling fee-based, transaction and flow-driven revenues.
Kotak is building a unified digital SME platform spanning sourcing, underwriting, credit and operations.

West Asia conflict escalation pushed crude oil prices toward USD 120 per barrel, reigniting inflationary pressures and prompting central bank rate hiking cycles, creating a challenging operating environment.
Elevated credit costs from microcredit and retail unsecured portfolios require a calibrated and risk-conscious approach to growth.
NIM compression expected to continue as the 100 bps repo rate cut cycle impacts loan yields repricing faster than deposit costs, with 63% of advances linked to repo rate.
Keep building market share in Tractor Finance, Commercial Vehicles, and Construction Equipment segments in a disciplined and consistent manner.
